front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** ("the Agency") operates as a licensed North Carolina Home Care Agency providing in-home aide services. It covers private-pay clients and clients served under Medicaid Personal Care Services (State Plan PCS and the CAP/DA waiver). The Agency is licensed by the NC Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), Division of Health Service Regulation (DHSR), Acute and Home Care Licensure and Certification Section, under G.S. 131E-135 to 131E-142 and 10A NCAC 13J.

The manual has four purposes:

1. **Meet the licensure requirement for written policies.** 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a) requires the governing body to adopt written policies on scope of services, admission and discharge, supervision, plan of care, emergency care in the home, record return timeframe, personnel qualifications, organizational chart, program evaluation, confidentiality and referrals. This manual contains those policies and the related administrative, client care and personnel policies that DHSR reviews.
2. **Protect clients.** The policies implement the Declaration of Home Care Clients' Rights (G.S. 131E-144.3) and related notice, complaint and confidentiality duties. Clients are entitled to dignity, privacy, participation in their plan of care, and freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation.
3. **Give staff one consistent reference.** Directors, supervisors, health care practitioners, in-home aides and office staff should be able to see what the Agency requires of them and who is responsible for each task.
4. **Support the Agency's DHSR review.** DHSR reviews policies, procedures and personnel documents during the initial survey and rechecks compliance at later inspections. DHSR may inspect at any time (10A NCAC 13J .0904) and must inspect each agency at least every 3 years (G.S. 131E-140). The manual is organized so a surveyor can find each required policy quickly.

### Scope of services

The Agency provides **in-home aide services involving hands-on care** (G.S. 131E-136(2), (3)). Companion, sitter, respite and homemaker services alone are "home assistance services" and count as home care only when combined with other home care services. Where this manual refers to companion, sitter or respite staff, it does so only because the Agency offers those services together with in-home aide services. Those staff are supervised under the separate rules in 10A NCAC 13J .1503 and .1504. Those rules do not replace the in-home aide requirements in 10A NCAC 13J .1001, .1107 and .1110.

### Important notice

This manual is a template. It does not become the Agency's policy until it has been customized, adopted by the governing body, and staff have been trained on it (see "How to Use This Manual"). It is not legal advice. The Agency remains responsible for complying with the statutes and rules as currently in effect.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### 1. Customize it before use

This manual contains placeholders in brackets, such as **[AGENCY NAME]**, **[DIRECTOR NAME]**, **[SERVICE SUPERVISOR NAME]**, **[COUNTY / GEOGRAPHIC SERVICE AREA]**, **[ADDRESS]** and **[DHSR HOTLINE NUMBER, confirm current number with DHSR]**. Before the manual is submitted or used:

- Replace every placeholder with the Agency's actual information.
- Review each policy against what the Agency actually does and delete or revise anything that does not apply. Examples are services the Agency does not offer, Medicaid programs it does not enroll in, and multiple-premises provisions if it has only one site.
- Do not leave policies in the manual that staff will not follow. DHSR measures the Agency against what its policies say.
- Name the geographic service area for each service in writing, as 10A NCAC 13J .1001(g) requires. The in-home aide service area is limited by 10A NCAC 13J .1107(h).

### 2. Adopt it through the governing body

The governing body must adopt the written policies (10A NCAC 13J .1001(a)). Record adoption in the governing body's minutes or a signed resolution showing the date, the version adopted and the signatures. Keep that record with the manual.

### 3. Keep it current

- Review the manual at least annually. The governing body's annual comprehensive program evaluation (10A NCAC 13J .1004) is a natural time to do so.
- Revise the manual when a statute, rule, DHSR guidance, Medicaid clinical coverage policy or Agency practice changes, and record the revision date and the governing body's approval. Track DHSR notices, including emergency rule waivers issued under G.S. 131E-112(a), (a1).
- Confirm with DHSR that the checklist version used for Appendix A is the latest before each submission. See Regulatory Framework.
- Give DHSR the written notices the rules require, such as ownership or name changes, new service categories, and expansions of the service area.
- Remove superseded versions from use. Keep a copy of prior versions according to the Agency's retention schedule.

### 4. Train staff on it

The Agency must train staff on the policies that apply to their jobs. This includes training on the clients' rights policies (G.S. 131E-144.5), infection control and bloodborne/airborne pathogen training (10A NCAC 13J .1003), and orientation and in-service education under the Agency's personnel policies (10A NCAC 13J .1003(d)). Staff should receive the manual or the relevant sections at orientation and again after material revisions. Keep signed acknowledgments and in-service attendance records in personnel files or training records.

### 5. Find what you need

- **Organization.** Following DHSR's guidance, the manual is organized in the order of the DHSR Home Care Initial Survey Checklist and grouped under its three headings: **Administrative Policies, Client Care Policies and Personnel Policies**. Each policy carries the rule cite printed on the checklist so a surveyor can check each line.
- **Appendix A (Official Checklist Crosswalk).** Appendix A lists every item on the official checklist and the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it as a completeness check before submission and as a finding aid during a survey.
- **Procedures and forms.** Policies state what the Agency requires. Procedures and forms explain who does what and when. Where a policy refers to a form (for example Form DHHS 3405 for TB screening), use the current version.

### 6. Responsibilities

The **governing body** adopts the policies and oversees compliance. The **agency director** is responsible for day-to-day implementation, including implementing the client Bill of Rights (G.S. 131E-144.5). The **service supervisor and health care practitioner** carry out the clinical supervision and plan-of-care policies. **All staff** must read and follow the policies that apply to their work and report concerns to their supervisor.

citations.title: Definitions (home care agency; home care services)
citations.requirement: Home care services include in-home aide services involving hands-on care. Companion, sitter, respite and homemaker alone are 'home assistance services' (G.S. 131E-136(1b)); they count as home care only when combined with other home care services.

citations.title: Licensure requirements
citations.requirement: No operating without a DHHS license. Nonrefundable annual fee is $510. License is issued only for the named premises and persons, is not transferable without written DHHS approval, and must be posted conspicuously on the premises.

citations.title: Deemed status for accredited agencies
citations.requirement: Commission rules deem an agency licensed without further review if it is accredited (e.g., Joint Commission, NLN, NC Accreditation Commission for In-Home Aide Services) for all services it provides.

citations.title: Rules and enforcement
citations.requirement: Rules must define in-home aide geographic service areas and staffing qualifications, bar hiring Health Care Personnel Registry listees, require owner training, and set advertising limits. DHSR inspects each agency at least every 3 years.

citations.title: Inspection; client record access; DHSR hotline notice
citations.requirement: Before releasing information or allowing record inspections, advise each client in writing of the right to object in writing. Give each client written notice of the DHSR hotline number before care or at the initial evaluation visit.

citations.title: Adverse action on a license
citations.requirement: DHHS may suspend, revoke, annul, withdraw, recall, cancel or amend a license for substantial failure to comply with Part 3 or its rules. Chapter 150B (APA) governs appeals.

citations.title: Unlicensed operation: penalties and injunction
citations.requirement: Knowingly operating without a license is a Class 3 misdemeanor (fine up to $500). DHHS must seek injunctions against unlicensed operation and may seek injunctive relief if a person hinders its duties.

citations.title: Smoking prohibited in client homes
citations.requirement: Agency must prohibit employees (including contractors) from smoking while providing services in a client's home and must tell clients of the prohibition. Administrative penalty up to $200 per violation.

citations.title: Declaration of home care clients' rights
citations.requirement: Fifteen client rights, including: plan-of-care participation; dignity and privacy; confidentiality; freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation; grievances without reprisal; written statement of charges; refuse services; on-call and supervisor access; 10-day license-action notice.

citations.title: Notice to client
citations.requirement: At the initial evaluation visit or before services, give each client the rights declaration, client-responsibility policies, agency complaint contact, and DHSR section address and phone. Keep signed receipts in agency files.

citations.title: Implementation of client rights
citations.requirement: The home care agency director is responsible for implementing the Bill of Rights. Each agency must provide appropriate training to implement it.

citations.title: Enforcement and investigation; agency complaint duty
citations.requirement: Agency must investigate client or family complaints within 72 hours and document the complaint and its resolution. DHSR starts investigations immediately (life-threatening), within 24 hours (abuse), 48 hours (neglect), 2 weeks (other).

citations.title: Confidentiality of records and complainants
citations.requirement: DHHS may inspect client records at the agency to investigate alleged violations. DHHS must keep complainants and inspected records confidential.

citations.title: Waiver of rules during emergencies
citations.requirement: During a declared state of emergency or disaster, DHSR may temporarily waive Commission rules for home care agencies. Agencies should track and follow DHSR waiver notices.

citations.title: Criminal history check of applicants
citations.requirement: Submit the criminal history check request within 5 business days of a conditional offer of employment (per DHSR Home Care FAQ, rev. 5/30/25).

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines ADLs, IADLs (including medication reminders), extensive vs. limited assistance, hands-on care, in-home aide services, plan of care, and 'health care practitioner' (G.S. 90-640(a)). Policies must use these terms.

citations.title: License
citations.requirement: Each agency premises must obtain its own license unless exempt under G.S. 131E-136(3).

citations.title: Application, issuance, posting
citations.requirement: Applicants with no prior home care ownership must complete DHSR-approved training before a license is issued. One-year license. Post the license and a door sign with the agency name. License is non-transferable.

citations.title: Notices to DHSR: ownership/name, new service, discontinued service
citations.requirement: Written notice at least 30 days before an ownership or name change, and 30 days before adding a service category. Notify DHSR in writing if a licensed service is discontinued or unavailable for 6 continuous months.

citations.title: Inspections
citations.requirement: Inspections may occur at any time. Allow immediate access to premises and records or the survey is terminated. File a plan of correction within 10 working days. DHSR may visit clients' homes with client permission.

citations.title: Multiple premises
citations.requirement: For multi-site operators, DHSR may sample-inspect and, on 72 hours' notice, require records (including personnel records) at the inspected site. Sites may share staff and centralize records.

citations.title: Compliance with laws
citations.requirement: Comply with all federal, state and local law, including Social Security Act 1128B and 42 USC 1320a-7a and 7b (false statements, kickbacks). Staff must hold current NC licenses/registrations. Accredited agencies send DHSR survey reports within 30 days.

citations.title: Adverse action
citations.requirement: DHSR may reduce a license to provisional or revoke it, including for any failure that endangers client health, safety or welfare. A provisional license must be posted in place of the full license. Appeals follow G.S. 150B.

citations.title: Required written policies
citations.requirement: Governing body must adopt written policies on 11 topics: scope of services; admission and discharge; supervision; plan of care; emergency care in the home; record return timeframe; personnel qualifications; org chart; program evaluation; confidentiality; referrals.

citations.title: Agency director and supervisor
citations.requirement: Director must be a health care practitioner, or have 2 years' home care/G.S. 131E or 122C management experience, or hold a bachelor's degree plus 1 year. Designate a service supervisor, document duties, and notify DHSR in writing within 5 working days of a vacancy.

citations.title: Responsibility for services; geographic service area policy
citations.requirement: Agency keeps ultimate responsibility for contracted services. Written policy must name the geographic area for each service. Give DHSR 30 days' written notice before expanding the service area without a new site.

citations.title: Administrative, financial and statistical records
citations.requirement: Keep the annual home care budget available for inspection. Keep statistical records (staff FTEs, client demographics, units of service). Retain these records at least 3 years. Keep home care finances separately identifiable if part of a larger entity.

citations.title: Infection control, OSHA and TB screening
citations.requirement: Written infection control/communicable disease policies consistent with 15A NCAC 19A and 29 CFR 1910. Hands-on staff need a baseline TB skin test; positives need noninfectious status before assignment. Use Form DHHS 3405.

citations.title: Health Care Personnel Registry bar
citations.requirement: Do not hire, directly or by contract, anyone with a substantiated finding on the NC Health Care Personnel Registry (G.S. 131E-256(a)(1)).

citations.title: Personnel policies and job descriptions
citations.requirement: Written policies on personnel record content, orientation and in-service education; keep in-service attendance records. Written job descriptions for every position. Assign staff only to duties they are trained, competent and licensed for. No hour counts are set.

citations.title: Personnel record contents and retention
citations.requirement: Per employee: application, signed job description, references, TB records, Hep B vaccine or declination, annual bloodborne/airborne training, annual evaluation, credential checks, competency verification. Keep 1 year after termination.

citations.title: RN-verified core competencies for aides not on the Nurse Aide Registry
citations.requirement: For aides hired after 4/1/2009 not on the registry, an RN must verify six core skills: mobility/transfers, bath/shower, toileting, dressing, eating, continence care.

citations.title: Evaluation (annual program evaluation; 90-day record review)
citations.requirement: Governing body does an annual comprehensive evaluation (clients served, hours, outcomes, staff adequacy, non-acceptances, discharge reasons) and reviews a sample of active and closed client records every 90 days. Document evaluators, methods and actions.

citations.title: Client rights and responsibilities
citations.requirement: Give each client written notice of rights and responsibilities before care or at the initial evaluation visit. Document that clients were informed (G.S. 131E-144.3), give G.S. 131E-144.4 notices, and comply with G.S. 131E-144.6(b).

citations.title: Acceptance of clients for service
citations.requirement: Written intake policies: staff adequacy and absence coverage, home suitability, family availability, scope and area, referral-source notice when needs can't be met, 48 hours' notice before reducing or ending service (listed exceptions), referral to other agencies.

citations.title: In-home aide services: plan of care, Nurse Aide Registry, permitted duties
citations.requirement: Plan of care signed by practitioner and client, copy kept in home, with assistance level per ADL. Aides giving extensive assistance must be on the Nurse Aide Registry. Aides may assist with self-administration of ordered medications and must report changes.

citations.title: Initial in-home assessment and practitioner availability
citations.requirement: Health care practitioner assesses in the client's home before the plan of care (social, mental, physical, environmental, economic, ADLs, IADLs), signed and dated. Practitioner must be available for supervision and consultation.

citations.title: Block grant agencies; in-home aide geographic limit
citations.requirement: In-home aide service area is limited to the agency's county, contiguous counties, or within 90 minutes' driving time, whichever is greater. HCCBG/SSBG agencies must also follow 10A NCAC 06A and 06X.

citations.title: Caregiver competency and delegated supervision
citations.requirement: Assign caregivers only tasks they have demonstrated to the health care practitioner, with documentation kept. Supervision may be delegated by agency policy only if the practitioner stays available and accountable.

citations.title: Supervisory visits
citations.requirement: Practitioner makes a supervisory visit to each client's home every 90 days (caregiver present or not), and annually while the caregiver is providing care. Record date, findings, signature. Document corrective action. Practitioner available during service hours.

citations.title: Arrangements for services with other agencies or individuals
citations.requirement: Contracted services need a signed written agreement with 10 listed terms (services, term, fees, licensure verification, supervision, equal personnel standards, documentation, geographic area). Review annually.

citations.title: Plan of care policies
citations.requirement: Written policies must ensure services and items to be provided are specified under a plan of care.

citations.title: Case review and plan of care
citations.requirement: Plan of care is built with the client and reviewed every 90 days by the practitioner. It must state service type, frequency and duration, restrictions, safety measures and goals. Notify the physician of changes if physician orders are required.

citations.title: Orders (when required for in-home aide services)
citations.requirement: When orders for in-home aide services are required, a prescriber signs them and the original goes in the client record. Care may begin on a verbal order in the interim.

citations.title: Service records: requirement
citations.requirement: Written record policies. Client name on every page, true entry dates, 'late entry' labeling. Originals stay secure on premises. Removed records return within 5 working days with a sign-out log. Retain 5 years after discharge (minors: until 3 years after age 18).

citations.title: Content of record
citations.requirement: Admission data (ID, signed rights form, next of kin, referral source, home assessment) and service data (initial assessment, goals, client approval, dated and signed service entries, discharge summary, coordination evidence).

citations.title: Companion/sitter/respite agency director
citations.requirement: Only for non-hands-on (companion, sitter, respite) services: director needs a high school diploma or GED plus health care practitioner status or 1 year of experience. Does not replace .1001 for in-home aide services.

citations.title: Supervision of companion, sitter and respite staff
citations.requirement: For non-hands-on staff: contact the client every 3 months and visit the home at least every 6 months, plus annually while the aide is in the home. Document each visit. Supervisor is available on-site when necessary.

citations.title: OSHA General Industry Standards
citations.requirement: 13J incorporates 29 CFR 1910 by reference. Infection control policies must comply with it, and hands-on staff need annual airborne and bloodborne pathogen training under the agency exposure control plan.

citations.title: State Plan Personal Care Services in In-Home Settings (amended Jan. 1, 2026)
citations.requirement: In-home PCS requires a service authorization for a set number of hours and an approved provider service plan. Do not schedule beyond authorized hours (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: NC CAP/DA waiver (Nov. 1, 2024 - Oct. 31, 2029)
citations.requirement: CAP/DA is the governing waiver for in-home aide services to adults at risk of institutionalization. Referrals and assessments run through NCLIFTSS (833-522-5429) (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Electronic visit verification for PCS and home health
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid PCS and CAP/DA visits. NC Medicaid expects at least 85% of visit data captured electronically (manual entries 15% or less). Sandata is the state vendor for NC Medicaid Direct (per fact-checked research).

policies.title: Agency Organization Chart and Governing Body Structure
policies.applies_to: Governing body, agency director, service supervisor/RN, scheduler/intake staff and all caregivers
policies.purpose: To define who governs [AGENCY NAME], who is accountable for daily operations and client services, and how authority flows, so that staff, clients and DHSR surveyors can see the lines of responsibility at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is governed by a governing body that adopts and approves the written policies required by 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a), including this organizational chart. The agency keeps a current organizational chart showing the governing body, the agency director, the service supervisor/registered nurse (RN), the scheduler/intake staff and the caregivers (in-home aides). The agency director is responsible for implementing the client Bill of Rights and for providing the training needed to do so (G.S. 131E-144.5). The chart is updated whenever the director or the service supervisor changes. This policy meets Supporting Documentation item .1001(8) — Agency Organization Chart, and item A(8) — 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a)(8), an organizational chart.

definitions.definition: The owner(s) or board of [AGENCY NAME] that holds legal responsibility for the agency, adopts its written policies and appoints the agency director.
The person who manages the daily operation of the agency, meets the director qualifications in ADM-04, and is responsible for implementing the client Bill of Rights.
The person designated in writing to supervise in-home aide services, develop and review plans of care and consult with caregivers (see ADM-06 and CLN-08).
A written diagram that shows each position, the name of the person holding it and who that person reports to.

procedures: The governing body, identified as [GOVERNING BODY / OWNER NAME(S)], adopts the written policies required by 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a) before the agency accepts its first client. Adoption is recorded in signed and dated governing body minutes or a written resolution.

The agency director prepares the organizational chart before the initial survey. The chart shows, from top to bottom: the governing body; the agency director; the service supervisor/RN; the scheduler/intake staff; and the caregivers (in-home aides).

The chart lists each position by title and the name of the current holder. It uses lines to show who reports to whom: caregivers report to the service supervisor/RN; the service supervisor/RN and the scheduler/intake staff report to the agency director; the agency director reports to the governing body.
The governing body reviews and approves the chart and signs and dates it. The approved chart is filed in the Policy & Procedure Manual and in the agency administrative file at [ADDRESS].
A copy of the chart is kept where it can be handed to a DHSR surveyor immediately on request during an unannounced inspection (see SUP-02).

When the director or the service supervisor changes, the agency director (or, if the director is the one leaving, the governing body) revises the chart on the date the change takes effect and no later than 5 working days afterward. The governing body re-approves the revised chart and the old version is kept, marked superseded, with its dates.
When the director position becomes vacant, the governing body also sends DHSR the written vacancy notice required by ADM-04 within 5 working days.
The agency director gives each new employee a copy of the current chart during orientation (PER-06) so staff know who supervises them and who to call.

The agency director carries out the client Bill of Rights as required by G.S. 131E-144.5. This includes making sure each client receives the rights statement at admission (CLN-01) and that complaints are handled under CLN-02.

The agency director provides appropriate Bill of Rights training to all staff at orientation and again during annual in-service education (PER-05). Attendance is recorded on a sign-in sheet that is kept in the personnel record.
When the agency director is absent, the qualified backup named in ADM-04 acts in the director's place. The scheduler/intake staff keep the backup's name and [PHONE] posted at the office.

The governing body reviews this policy and the chart at least annually and whenever the agency adds a position or changes its structure. The review is recorded under ADM-16 (Policy Review and Document Control).
If ownership or the agency name changes, the governing body follows the DHSR notice steps in SUP-02 and revises the chart before the change takes effect.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the written policies required by 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a), approves and signs the chart, appoints the director and the service supervisor, and reviews the structure at least annually.
Prepares and updates the chart, implements the client Bill of Rights, ensures staff Bill of Rights training and notifies the governing body of any change in key positions.
Supervises caregivers per the chart, and confirms that the chart reflects current supervisory assignments.
Know the reporting lines, use the chart to route concerns and keep the backup director contact information current at the office.

documentation: Signed and dated current organizational chart
Superseded charts with effective dates
Governing body minutes or resolution adopting the .1001(a) policies
Bill of Rights training sign-in sheets
Annual policy review record (ADM-16)

policies.title: Licensure, License Posting, Notices to DHSR, Inspections and Plan of Correction
policies.applies_to: Governing body, agency director, service supervisor/RN, office staff and all employees who may be present during a DHSR inspection
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] operates only with a valid North Carolina home care agency license, posts it as required, gives DHSR the notices the rules require, and cooperates fully with inspections and corrects any deficiency on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not provide home care services without a current license issued by the NC Department of Health and Human Services (G.S. 131E-138). The in-home aide services the agency provides are home care services under G.S. 131E-136. Companion, sitter, respite or homemaker services provided alone are home assistance services, and they count as home care only when combined with other home care services. The license is valid only for the named premises and persons, is not transferable without written DHHS approval, and expires at midnight on December 31 of each year. The annual fee is $510 and is nonrefundable. The agency posts the license conspicuously on the premises, together with a door sign showing the agency name, and posts a provisional license in place of the full license if DHSR issues one (10A NCAC 13J .0903 and .0907). The agency gives DHSR written notice of ownership changes, name changes, new service categories and discontinued services. It allows DHSR to inspect at any time and files a written plan of correction within 10 working days of receiving a statement of deficiencies.

definitions.definition: The NC DHHS Division of Health Service Regulation, Acute and Home Care Licensure and Certification Section, which licenses and inspects home care agencies. Phone 919-855-4620; email DHSR.homecare@dhhs.nc.gov.

In-home aide services involving hands-on care, and other services defined in G.S. 131E-136. Companion, sitter, respite and homemaker services alone are home assistance services and count as home care only when combined with other home care services.
A license DHSR may issue in place of a full license when it reduces the license status under 10A NCAC 13J .0907. It must be posted in place of the full license.
The agency's written response to cited deficiencies, stating what will be corrected, how, by whom and by when.
A weekday that is not a State holiday.

procedures: The governing body confirms that no client is accepted and no service is provided until the license has been issued for the named premises ([ADDRESS]) and the named persons. Knowingly operating without a license is a Class 3 misdemeanor (G.S. 131E-141.1), and DHHS must seek an injunction against unlicensed operation (G.S. 131E-142).

Before a license is issued, an owner who has no prior home care ownership completes the DHSR-approved home care provider training and sends the completion proof to DHSR (10A NCAC 13J .0903). The agency director files the certificate in the administrative file.

The agency obtains a separate license for each agency premises unless an exemption applies under G.S. 131E-136(3) (10A NCAC 13J .0902). For multiple sites, the agency may share staff and centralize records, and the director keeps personnel records retrievable.

The agency director posts the license in a conspicuous place at the office and installs a door sign showing the agency name. The director checks the posting at the start of each month and records the check.
If DHSR issues a provisional license, the director posts it in place of the full license on the day it is received and tells the governing body in writing the same day.

The director tracks the December 31 expiration date. The renewal application and the $510 fee are sent to DHSR in time to be received on or before December 31 each year, and the director records the date mailed or submitted. A license issued during the year still expires on December 31, so the agency budgets for a first renewal payment in the year it is issued.
The agency never transfers the license. Before any sale or transfer of ownership, the governing body requests written DHHS approval as required by G.S. 131E-138.

The governing body gives DHSR written notice at least 30 days before an ownership change or a change in the agency name (10A NCAC 13J .0903). The director keeps a copy of the notice and proof of delivery.

Before adding a new service category, the governing body gives DHSR written notice at least 30 days ahead. The agency does not offer or advertise the new service until the notice period has run and DHSR requirements are met (see ADM-01).
If a licensed service is discontinued or unavailable for 6 continuous months, the director notifies DHSR in writing and records the date the service stopped.

The agency treats every inspection as unannounced. Whoever is at the office when surveyors arrive asks for identification, calls the director or the backup director immediately, and gives surveyors immediate access to the premises and records. Refusing access causes the survey to be terminated, which may lead to adverse action.

The director or the designated backup accompanies the surveyors, answers questions, and provides personnel, client and administrative records as requested. If the agency operates multiple sites and DHSR requires records from another site, including personnel records, the director delivers them to the inspected site within 72 hours of DHSR's notice (10A NCAC 13J .0905).
When DHSR asks to visit a client's home, staff first ask the client for permission and respect the client's decision. Staff do not pressure clients about whether to allow a visit.

Within 3 working days of receiving a statement of deficiencies, the director meets with the service supervisor/RN to assign corrective actions. The director files a written plan of correction with DHSR within 10 working days (10A NCAC 13J .0904).
The director follows up on each corrective action, records the completion date and keeps evidence (training sign-in sheets, revised policies, revised forms) in the inspection file.

The governing body reviews the survey results at its next meeting. If DHSR proposes adverse action (suspension, revocation, provisional license or other action under G.S. 131E-139 or 10A NCAC 13J .0907), the governing body decides on any appeal, which follows G.S. Chapter 150B.

The director keeps all DHSR correspondence, licenses, renewal records, notices and inspection reports in a permanent licensure file. DHSR inspects each agency at least every 3 years, so the agency stays survey-ready at all times and does not wait for a scheduled visit.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the license is current, approves ownership or name changes and new services, authorizes notices to DHSR and decides on any appeal of adverse action.
Posts the license and door sign, tracks the December 31 renewal, sends notices, hosts inspections and files the plan of correction within 10 working days.
Assists with inspections of client and clinical records and carries out clinical corrective actions.
Give surveyors immediate access, call the director at once and never turn a surveyor away.

documentation: Current license and provisional license (if any), with posting log
Home care provider training completion certificate
Renewal applications, fee receipts and dates received
Written notices to DHSR with proof of delivery (ownership, name, new service, discontinued service)
Survey reports, statements of deficiencies and dated plans of correction with evidence of completion
Correspondence on any adverse action or appeal

policies.title: Scope of Services
policies.applies_to: Governing body, agency director, service supervisor/RN, intake staff and all caregivers
policies.purpose: To state exactly which services [AGENCY NAME] is licensed to provide and which it does not provide, so that clients, staff, referral sources and surveyors share one clear understanding.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides in-home aide services under its North Carolina home care agency license [and companion, sitter and respite services — include only if licensed for these categories]. Services are provided in the client's home on a plan of care. The agency uses the terms defined in 10A NCAC 13J .0901 in all documents: activities of daily living (ADLs), instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs), limited assistance, extensive assistance and hands-on care. Aides may assist with self-administration of ordered medications and must report changes in the client's condition, as allowed by 10A NCAC 13J .1107. The agency does not provide skilled nursing services or medication administration. The agency advertises only the services it is licensed to provide. This policy meets Administrative Policies item .1001(a)(1) — Scope of Services policy, and item A(1) — 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a)(1), a description of the scope of services offered.

definitions.definition: Basic self-care tasks as defined in 10A NCAC 13J .0901, such as bathing, dressing, toileting, mobility/transferring, eating and personal hygiene.
Home-management tasks as defined in 10A NCAC 13J .0901, such as meal preparation, housekeeping, laundry, shopping and medication reminders.
The client performs most of the task and the aide provides help or hands-on support as defined in 10A NCAC 13J .0901.
The aide performs a major part of the task or the client cannot take part, as defined in 10A NCAC 13J .0901. Aides giving extensive assistance must be on the Nurse Aide Registry.
Direct physical contact by an aide while assisting a client with ADLs, as defined in 10A NCAC 13J .0901.
Hands-on personal care and home management services furnished by aides in the client's home under a plan of care, as defined in 10A NCAC 13J .0901.

procedures: The governing body adopts the list of licensed service categories below. The agency lists [IN-HOME AIDE SERVICES] and, only if licensed, [COMPANION / SITTER / RESPITE SERVICES]. The agency director confirms the list matches the license posted at the office (SUP-02).

In-home aide services include assistance with ADLs at the limited or extensive level. These include bathing, dressing, grooming and personal hygiene, toileting and incontinence care, mobility and transferring, and eating assistance. They also include assistance with IADLs, including meal preparation, light housekeeping, laundry, shopping and medication reminders, as directed by the plan of care.
The service supervisor/RN writes the assistance level (limited or extensive) for each ADL in the plan of care. Only tasks listed in the plan of care are performed (CLN-06).

Aides assist with self-administration of medications ordered by a health care practitioner and must report changes in the client's condition to the service supervisor/RN promptly (CLN-13, CLN-20). Aides do not administer medications.

The agency does not provide skilled nursing services, medication administration, injections, wound care, sterile procedures, tube feedings or other tasks that require a nursing license. Intake staff tell referral sources and clients this at the first contact and refer the person elsewhere if those services are needed (CLN-03, CLN-04).

Companion, sitter, respite or homemaker services alone are home assistance services. The agency provides them only when combined with other home care services under its license, or, if licensed only for those services, under the director standard in ADM-05.

The agency assigns each caregiver only to tasks that the caregiver is trained for, has been found competent to perform and is licensed or listed to perform. For extensive assistance, the aide must be on the Nurse Aide Registry (PER-01, PER-02).

The agency director reviews all brochures, website pages, social media, rate sheets and other advertising before use. Advertising must not claim any service that the agency is not licensed to provide or does not offer, and must name the agency as it appears on the license.
Before adding a service category, the governing body gives DHSR written notice 30 days ahead and revises this policy before the service starts (SUP-02).
Intake staff give each prospective client a written summary of the services provided and not provided. The service agreement repeats the scope (CLN-18).
Each time the agency discontinues a service or it is unavailable for 6 continuous months, the director notifies DHSR in writing and updates this policy (SUP-02).
The agency director reviews the scope of services annually as part of the program evaluation (ADM-08) and after any change in the license, rule or service offered. Revisions are logged under ADM-16.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the scope of services and any change to licensed categories.
Keeps the scope consistent with the license, approves all advertising and ensures staff and clients understand the scope.
Matches the plan of care to the scope and sets the assistance level for each ADL.
Explain the scope to inquirers, and refer them elsewhere when the requested service is outside it.
Perform only tasks listed in the plan of care and within their training and competence.

documentation: Approved scope of services statement listing licensed categories and exclusions
Written summary given to clients and the signed service agreement
Approved advertising file with director sign-off and dates
Written notices to DHSR for added or discontinued services
Policy revision log (ADM-16)

policies.title: Emergency Care in the Home and Emergency Preparedness
policies.applies_to: All caregivers, service supervisor/RN, scheduler/intake staff and agency director
policies.purpose: To make sure that caregivers respond correctly to a medical or other emergency in a client's home and that the agency can keep services going, or safely adjust them, during severe weather, disasters or staff shortages.
policies.policy: Caregivers of [AGENCY NAME] call 911 in any medical emergency, stay with the client, notify the service supervisor/RN and the family or representative, and document the event. An RN is on call for consultation during all hours aide services are provided. The agency keeps a client-level disaster plan and a continuity plan for staff absence. During a declared state of emergency or disaster, the agency follows any DHSR rule-waiver notices issued under G.S. 131E-112. This policy meets Administrative Policies item .1001(5) — Emergency preparedness, and item A(5) — 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a)(5), management of emergency care situations in the home.

definitions.definition: A sudden condition that could threaten life or cause serious harm, such as unresponsiveness, chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, serious bleeding, a major fall or injury, choking, or a seizure that does not stop.
A registered nurse available by phone for supervision and consultation during all hours aide services are provided.
A written plan for an individual client that states how that client will be served or contacted during a disaster, including who to call and where the client will go if evacuation is needed.
The agency's plan for covering a client's visits when a caregiver is absent (see CLN-19).

procedures: Each caregiver receives training on this policy at orientation (PER-06) and again during in-service education (PER-05). The training covers recognizing emergencies, calling 911, how to reach the on-call RN, and how to document.
In a medical emergency, the caregiver calls 911 first. The caregiver gives the address, the client's name and condition, and follows the dispatcher's instructions.

The caregiver stays with the client until emergency responders arrive and take over. The caregiver gives only first aid that the caregiver has been trained to give and that is within the aide's permitted duties (CLN-13). If the client has a valid out-of-hospital do-not-resuscitate order, the caregiver shows it to responders if it is in the home.
The caregiver calls the service supervisor/RN or the on-call RN right after calling 911. The call is made from the home if possible, and the supervisor/RN gives guidance and begins follow-up.

The service supervisor/RN or the caregiver notifies the client's family, representative or listed emergency contact. The supervisor/RN also notifies the referral source and any case manager as the plan of care or program rules require.

Within 24 hours the caregiver completes an incident report (CLN-15) and a visit note stating what happened, the time, who was called, what was done and who took over care. The supervisor/RN reviews the report the same day or the next working day.

The service supervisor/RN informs the agency director the same day of any emergency involving injury, hospitalization or death. The director determines whether any reporting is required under CLN-14, CLN-15 or CLN-11.

The service supervisor/RN reviews the plan of care after any emergency or hospitalization and documents any change in the client's condition or needs (CLN-20). Aides do not resume care at an altered level until the supervisor/RN has reviewed the case.

The agency keeps an on-call schedule showing the RN available during all hours of aide services. The agency director posts the schedule at the office and gives all caregivers the on-call [PHONE] number in writing.

At admission, the service supervisor/RN records each client's emergency contacts, physician or practitioner, known medical conditions, medication list and any special needs, and keeps a copy in the home with the plan of care so responders can see it.

For each client, the service supervisor/RN prepares a client-level disaster plan during the initial assessment (CLN-05). It identifies whether the client can evacuate, who will help, whether the client relies on electricity-dependent equipment and how the agency will check on the client.

Before a forecasted storm or other hazard, the scheduler/intake staff review the schedule and contact high-risk clients, those who live alone or depend on equipment, to confirm their plan. Contacts and outcomes are logged.

During a disaster, the agency director decides whether visits are made, delayed or replaced by phone contact. Caregiver safety is a factor and no caregiver is required to travel under unsafe road conditions (CLN-22). The agency tells affected clients and their families of any change and records the contact.

When a caregiver is absent, the scheduler/intake staff follow the continuity plan: contact another qualified caregiver, tell the client and family, and tell the service supervisor/RN if no replacement is available (CLN-19). The agency does not leave a client without needed care without notifying the client and supervisor.

The agency director tracks the DHSR website and email for rule-waiver notices during any declared state of emergency or disaster (G.S. 131E-112). If a waiver applies, the director documents which rule is waived, the dates and how the agency changed practice, and keeps the notice on file.
The agency director reviews emergency events and drills as part of the annual program evaluation (ADM-08) and updates this policy and the disaster plans as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Call 911 in emergencies, stay with the client, notify the supervisor/RN, document the event and follow the disaster plan.
Remain available for consultation during all aide hours, notify the family and director, review the plan of care and prepare client-level disaster plans.
Maintain the on-call schedule, contact high-risk clients before hazards and cover absences.
Decides on service changes during disasters, follows DHSR waiver notices and ensures training and annual review.

documentation: Incident report and visit note for each emergency (CLN-15)
On-call RN schedule
Client emergency contact sheet and client-level disaster plan in each client record
Pre-storm client contact log
DHSR waiver notices received and the agency's response
Emergency training sign-in sheets

policies.title: Geographic Service Area
policies.applies_to: Governing body, agency director, intake and scheduling staff
policies.purpose: To identify the specific geographic area where [AGENCY NAME] provides each licensed service, and to make sure intake and scheduling stay within that area.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides in-home aide services in [COUNTY] County and in the contiguous counties of [LIST CONTIGUOUS COUNTIES], or within 90 minutes' driving time of the agency office at [ADDRESS], whichever is greater (10A NCAC 13J .1107(h)). [If licensed for companion/sitter/respite services, state the area for those services here.] The agency does not accept clients whose homes are outside this area. The agency gives DHSR 30 days' written notice before expanding its service area without a new site (10A NCAC 13J .1001(g)). This policy meets Administrative Policies item .1001(g) / .1107(h) — Geographic Service Area; In-home Aide Services, and item G — 10A NCAC 13J .1001(g), written policies which identify the specific geographic area in which the agency provides each service.

definitions.definition: The area in which the agency has told DHSR it provides a given licensed service.
Counties that share a border with the agency's home county.
The estimated time to drive by road from the agency office to the client's home under normal traffic, determined with a mapping tool at intake.

procedures: The governing body adopts the service area for each licensed service and records it in the minutes. For in-home aide services, the area is the agency's county, its contiguous counties, or within 90 minutes' driving time of the agency, whichever is greater.

The agency director prepares a service area map or list that names each county and any additional area covered by the 90-minute driving time. The director keeps the map at the intake desk and in the Policy & Procedure Manual.
For each referral, intake staff record the client's full address and screen it against the service area before the agency accepts the client (CLN-04).

If the address is within the county or a contiguous county, intake staff record that it is within the service area. If not, intake staff use a mapping tool to estimate driving time from the agency office. The result is printed or saved in the intake file.

If the address is outside the service area, intake staff do not accept the referral. They tell the referral source and the client or family the same day that the agency cannot serve the address, and offer information about other agencies (CLN-03, CLN-04). The decision is logged.

The agency director reviews any borderline case, such as a driving time close to 90 minutes in poor weather, before acceptance. The director considers whether the agency can provide reliable staffing and absence coverage for the address.
The scheduler/intake staff schedule caregivers so that travel does not cause late or missed visits (CLN-19). The service supervisor/RN reports any area where late visits are frequent to the director.
If a client moves outside the service area, the service supervisor/RN and the director follow the discharge and transfer steps in CLN-10, including notice to the client and help with referrals.

Before the agency expands its service area without adding a new site, the governing body sends DHSR written notice at least 30 days before the expansion starts. The director keeps proof of delivery. The agency does not serve clients in the expanded area until the 30 days have passed.
When the agency adds a new site, it obtains the license needed for that site under SUP-02 before serving the area.

If the agency receives funding that has its own service area rules, such as a Home and Community Care Block Grant or Social Services Block Grant, the director also follows those program rules, 10A NCAC 06A and 06X, and records which rules apply. The agency follows the more restrictive rule.
The director reviews the service area annually during the program evaluation (ADM-08), and revises this policy under ADM-16 whenever the area changes.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the service area and approves any expansion.
Maintains the service area map, decides borderline cases, and sends the 30-day written notice to DHSR before expansion.
Screen each address before acceptance and document the result.
Schedules within the service area and reports travel problems.
Considers area and staffing during the initial assessment and reports travel-related service problems.

documentation: Governing body minutes adopting the service area
Service area map or county list
Intake address screening record and driving-time result
Log of referrals declined for being outside the area
30-day written notice to DHSR and proof of delivery (if the area is expanded)

policies.title: Agency Director: Qualifications, Job Description and Vacancy Notice
policies.applies_to: Governing body, agency director and backup director
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is managed by a qualified agency director with documented duties, that a qualified backup is available, and that DHSR is told promptly when the director position is vacant.
policies.policy: The agency director of [AGENCY NAME] must meet one of the qualifications in 10A NCAC 13J .1001(b): a health care practitioner, or at least 2 years of supervisory or management experience in home care or another provider licensed under G.S. Chapter 131E or 122C, or a bachelor's degree in health, business or public administration science plus 1 year of supervisory or management experience in home care or another licensed health care program. The agency keeps a written job description for the director and documentation of the director's qualifications. The governing body notifies DHSR in writing within 5 working days of a director vacancy. A qualified backup director is named in advance. This policy meets Administrative Policies item .1001(b)(d)(e) — Agency Director job description.

definitions.definition: A person defined in 10A NCAC 13J .0901 by reference to G.S. 90-640(a).
Experience directing staff or operations in a home care agency or another provider licensed under G.S. Chapter 131E or 122C, shown by employer letters, job descriptions or similar proof.
A person named in writing who meets the director qualifications and who acts as director when the director is absent or the position is vacant.
A period in which no person who meets this policy's qualifications holds the director position.

procedures: The governing body appoints the agency director in writing and confirms that the person meets at least one of the three qualification paths in 10A NCAC 13J .1001(b) before the person starts. The appointment is recorded in the minutes.

The governing body obtains proof of qualification for the path claimed: a copy of the health care practitioner license and its current status; or written verification of at least 2 years of supervisory or management experience from prior employers; or a copy of the degree transcript or diploma plus written verification of 1 year of supervisory or management experience.
The proof is checked for dates, titles and the type of licensed program. The reviewer signs and dates the verification and files it in the director's personnel record (PER-03).

The governing body approves a written director job description and gives the director a signed copy (ADM-07). The job description states that the director: manages the daily operation of the agency; implements the client Bill of Rights (SUP-01); ensures compliance with licensure rules; hires, orients and evaluates staff; designates and oversees the service supervisor; handles complaints; oversees quality improvement and the annual evaluation; and acts as the contact for DHSR.
The director signs the job description to show understanding, and the governing body reviews it annually at the time of the director's performance evaluation (PER-04).

The governing body names a backup director who meets the same qualifications, and records the name and [PHONE] in the policy manual. The backup acts as director during any absence and is told of the duties in writing.
The agency director designates the service supervisor in writing and documents the supervisor's duties, as required by 10A NCAC 13J .1001 (ADM-06).
If the director leaves, is removed or becomes unable to serve, the governing body immediately names the backup as acting director so that the agency is never without a qualified person in charge.

Within 5 working days of the vacancy, the governing body sends DHSR a written notice of the vacancy. The notice states the date the position became vacant, the name of the acting director and the expected date a permanent director will be appointed. A copy and the proof of delivery are kept in the licensure file (SUP-02).

The governing body recruits a replacement director who meets the qualifications. Once the replacement is appointed, the governing body follows steps 1 to 5, sends DHSR written notice of the new director's name and revises the organizational chart (SUP-01).
The governing body reviews the director's qualification file at least annually and when this policy is reviewed under ADM-16 to confirm any license is current.

If a director qualified through a practitioner license and that license lapses or is restricted, the governing body treats the position as vacant unless another qualification path is documented, and follows steps 8 to 10.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the director, verifies qualifications, approves the job description, names the backup and sends the 5-working-day vacancy notice to DHSR.
Performs the duties of the job description, keeps qualification proof current and designates the service supervisor.
Acts as director during absence or vacancy and meets the same qualifications.

documentation: Signed and dated director appointment
Proof of qualification (license, employer verification or degree transcript plus experience verification)
Signed director job description
Written designation of the backup director
Written vacancy notice to DHSR and proof of delivery
Annual review of the director file

policies.title: Director Standard for Companion/Sitter/Respite-Only Services (If Applicable)
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Director and Service Supervisor. Applies only if [AGENCY NAME] offers non-hands-on companion, sitter or respite services.
policies.purpose: To state the director and supervision standard that applies to companion, sitter and respite services that involve no hands-on care. To make clear that this standard does not replace the director standard for in-home aide services.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Administrative Policies item .1503(1)a-b, Companion Sitter Agency Director (if applicable), 10A NCAC 13J .1503.

[AGENCY NAME] is licensed as a home care agency to provide in-home aide services, which include hands-on personal care. Because of that, the director standard in 10A NCAC 13J .1001 applies. It is set out in ADM-04. The lighter director standard in 10A NCAC 13J .1503 does NOT replace .1001 for any in-home aide service and may not be used to qualify the director of this agency. This policy is kept as a reference. It becomes operative only if the governing body approves a separate line of non-hands-on companion, sitter or respite services.

Under G.S. 131E-136(1b), (2) and (3), companion, sitter, respite and homemaker services alone are 'home assistance services'. They count as home care only when combined with other home care services such as in-home aide services. [AGENCY NAME] therefore treats any client who receives both hands-on care and companion/sitter/respite care as an in-home aide client. That client is covered by the full in-home aide policies (ADM-06, CLN-05, CLN-06, CLN-08).

Where an agency or a defined service line provides ONLY non-hands-on companion, sitter or respite services, the director must hold a high school diploma or GED plus either status as a health care practitioner or at least one year of experience. Non-hands-on staff are supervised on the schedule in 10A NCAC 13J .1504: client contact at least every 3 months, a home visit at least every 6 months, and an annual visit while the aide is in the home. Each contact or visit is documented. The supervisor is available on-site when necessary.

[AGENCY NAME] does not allow a companion, sitter or respite aide to perform hands-on personal care. A hands-on task requires a change in the service plan under CLN-06, a qualified assessment, a demonstrated competency and supervision under the in-home aide policies.

definitions.definition: Services that provide presence, supervision, social interaction or relief to a caregiver and do not include hands-on personal care.
The statutory term in G.S. 131E-136(1b) for companion, sitter, respite and homemaker services. They are home care only when combined with other home care services.
Home care services that involve hands-on personal care, for which this agency is licensed.
A person licensed in North Carolina to practice in a health care profession and qualified under 10A NCAC 13J to meet the standard being applied.

procedures: The governing body confirms and records in its minutes that [AGENCY NAME] is licensed for in-home aide services and that the .1001 director standard (ADM-04) applies to the director.
The Agency Director does not use the .1503 standard to qualify for the director position. The governing body verifies the director's credentials under ADM-04 before appointment.
Before any non-hands-on-only service line is offered, the governing body reviews this policy, approves the service line in writing and updates ADM-01 (Scope of Services).
The Agency Director notifies DHSR of any change in scope of services as required under SUP-02 before the new service line starts.

For a non-hands-on-only line, the governing body verifies and files proof that the director holds a high school diploma or GED plus either health care practitioner status or 1 year of experience. A copy of the diploma or GED, the license or reference letters is kept in the personnel file.
At intake, the Service Supervisor screens every referral for hands-on needs (bathing, toileting, transfers, feeding, dressing, personal hygiene) using the CLN-04 intake screen.

If a hands-on need is present or is likely to arise, the client is accepted only as an in-home aide client. The RN assessment (CLN-05) and plan of care (CLN-06) are completed before any service starts.
The scheduler records the service type on each client's service plan. Companion, sitter or respite aides receive written assignment sheets that list only non-hands-on tasks.
Aides report any request for or need of hands-on care to the Service Supervisor the same day. They do not perform the task.
The Service Supervisor contacts each non-hands-on client by telephone or in person at least every 3 months and documents the date, the contact method, the client's comments and any follow-up.

The Service Supervisor visits each non-hands-on client's home at least every 6 months and also once a year while the aide is in the home. The visit is documented with the date, observations, client satisfaction and any corrective action.

The Service Supervisor reports any change in the client's condition that suggests a need for hands-on care to the RN. The RN reassesses the client under CLN-20 and the service is moved to the in-home aide policies if needed.
The Service Supervisor is available on-site when necessary, and the on-call number [PHONE] is given to every non-hands-on client and aide.

The Agency Director reports the number of non-hands-on clients, the supervision contacts and visits made, and the corrections made to the governing body in the annual program evaluation (ADM-08) and the 90-day record review (ADM-09).

responsibilities.duty: Approves any non-hands-on service line, verifies that the correct director standard is applied, and records its decisions.
Meets the .1001 standard for in-home aide services, ensures non-hands-on services are not mixed with hands-on care, and reports to DHSR when scope changes.
Screens referrals, completes the 3-month contacts and 6-month and annual visits, and documents each one.
Performs only non-hands-on tasks and reports any need for hands-on care to the Service Supervisor the same day.

documentation: Governing body minutes showing the licensed scope and any approval of a non-hands-on service line
Director qualification file (diploma or GED, license or experience verification)
Intake screen showing hands-on need or no hands-on need
3-month client contact log and 6-month and annual supervisory visit reports
Aide assignment sheets listing non-hands-on tasks only

policies.title: Service Supervisor Designation and Job Description
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Director, Service Supervisor/RN, any delegated health care practitioner, and in-home aides
policies.purpose: To make sure a qualified Service Supervisor is designated, that the supervisor's duties are written down, that a registered nurse is available for supervision and consultation during all hours aide services are provided, and that DHSR is notified of any vacancy within 5 working days.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Administrative Policies item .1001(c)(d), Service Supervisor job description, 10A NCAC 13J .1001(b)-(e).

[AGENCY NAME] designates a Service Supervisor in writing. The governing body or Agency Director signs the designation, and the duties are documented in the job description below. The supervisor is a registered nurse licensed in North Carolina, because for in-home aide services an RN must be available for supervision and consultation during all hours aide services are provided and must make the home visit that develops the plan of care. In keeping with DHSR guidance, a licensed practical nurse (LPN) may not perform assessments or supervisory visits for in-home aide services at [AGENCY NAME].

A health care practitioner must be available for supervision and consultation at all times when services are provided (10A NCAC 13J .1107(d)-(f)). Supervision may be delegated to another qualified person by this written policy only if the health care practitioner stays available and accountable (10A NCAC 13J .1110(a)-(b)). In-home aides are assigned only tasks they have demonstrated to the health care practitioner, and the demonstration is documented and kept.

If the Service Supervisor position becomes vacant, [AGENCY NAME] notifies DHSR in writing within 5 working days of the vacancy. The agency covers the supervision duties with a qualified RN until a replacement is designated, so that no aide services are provided without an available RN.

SERVICE SUPERVISOR JOB DESCRIPTION. Reports to: Agency Director. Qualifications: current, unrestricted North Carolina RN license; experience and training in home care or community health that the governing body finds adequate; ability to assess clients in their homes and to teach and supervise aides. Responsibilities: (1) perform the initial in-home assessment before the plan of care (CLN-05); (2) develop, sign and review the plan of care, including the 90-day review (CLN-06); (3) assign aides only tasks they have demonstrated to the RN and for which they are competent (PER-02); (4) make supervisory visits and document them (CLN-08); (5) be available to aides and clients for consultation at all times aide services are provided; (6) evaluate changes in client condition and respond to incidents (CLN-15, CLN-20); (7) take part in orientation, in-service education and competency validation of aides; (8) take part in the 90-day record review and the annual program evaluation (ADM-08, ADM-09); (9) report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation under CLN-14 and refer findings under CLN-11; (10) coordinate with other agencies and practitioners (CLN-03, CLN-09).

definitions.definition: The registered nurse designated in writing by [AGENCY NAME] to supervise in-home aide services, assess clients, develop plans of care and be available for consultation.
The licensed professional (an RN at this agency) who assesses clients, supervises aides and stays accountable for supervision.
Supervision assigned to another qualified person under this written policy. The health care practitioner stays available and accountable.
Any period when no designated, qualified Service Supervisor is in place.

procedures: The governing body appoints the Service Supervisor in writing before the agency accepts its first in-home aide client. The appointment letter names the RN and the effective date.

Before the start date, the Agency Director verifies the RN's license through the NC Board of Nursing, checks for restrictions or discipline, and files a printout of the verification in the personnel file.
The Service Supervisor reviews and signs the job description in this policy and any updates. The signed copy is kept in the personnel file (see ADM-07).

The Agency Director posts a schedule showing which RN is available for consultation during every hour that aide services are scheduled, with a telephone number ([PHONE]). The scheduler gives the schedule to all aides.
If an alternate RN covers for the Service Supervisor, the alternate is named on the coverage schedule, verified as an NC-licensed RN and briefed on open client issues.
Only an RN performs initial in-home assessments and supervisory visits. The scheduler does not assign these tasks to an LPN, even if the LPN offers to help.

The Service Supervisor may delegate non-clinical tasks, such as scheduling, record filing and reminders, to staff named in the delegation list. The RN stays available and accountable for the supervision of aides and for all clinical decisions.
Any delegation of supervision tasks is written in the delegation list approved by the Agency Director, naming the person, the tasks and the review date. The list is reviewed at least annually.
The Service Supervisor documents each aide task demonstration (date, task, client or lab setting, result) and files it in the aide's personnel record.
If the Service Supervisor gives notice, resigns, is terminated or becomes unable to serve, the Agency Director immediately designates a qualified interim RN and informs the governing body.

The Agency Director sends written notice of the vacancy to DHSR, Acute and Home Care Licensure and Certification Section (email DHSR.homecare@dhhs.nc.gov or mail to [ADDRESS]) within 5 working days of the vacancy date. A copy of the notice and proof of sending are filed in the licensure file.
The Agency Director sends written notice to DHSR when the new Service Supervisor is designated, and files the new appointment letter, license verification and signed job description.
The governing body reviews the Service Supervisor's performance annually as part of PER-04 and reviews the adequacy of RN coverage in the annual program evaluation (ADM-08).
During the 90-day record review (ADM-09), the reviewer confirms that assessments, plan-of-care reviews and supervisory visits were done by an RN.

responsibilities.duty: Designates the Service Supervisor in writing and ensures RN coverage during all service hours.
Verifies the RN's license, keeps the coverage schedule, and notifies DHSR in writing within 5 working days of a vacancy.
Performs the duties in the job description above and remains available and accountable for supervision and consultation.
Never assigns assessments or supervisory visits to an LPN, and follows the RN coverage schedule.

documentation: Written designation of the Service Supervisor
Signed Service Supervisor job description
RN license verification
RN availability and coverage schedule
Delegation list, if any
Aide task demonstration records
Copy and proof of delivery of the 5-working-day vacancy notice to DHSR

policies.title: Job Descriptions for All Positions
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Director, Service Supervisor, scheduler/intake staff, in-home aides, and all other staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every position at [AGENCY NAME] has a written job description with qualifications and specific responsibilities, and that staff are assigned only duties they are trained, competent and licensed to perform.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Administrative Policies item .1003(e), Job Descriptions for other positions, and item 1003(e), Job descriptions for every position in writing, including qualifications and specific responsibilities, 10A NCAC 13J .1003(e).

[AGENCY NAME] maintains a written job description for every position, including the Agency Director, the RN/Service Supervisor, the scheduler/intake coordinator, the in-home aide, and any other position (for example billing or administrative staff). Each job description states the position title, the person to whom the position reports, minimum qualifications (education, licensure or certification, experience), and specific responsibilities.

Staff are assigned only duties they are trained, competent and licensed to perform. An aide may not be assigned a task until it has been demonstrated to the RN and documented (PER-02, CLN-13). A person whose license is required for a task is not assigned it unless the license is current.

Each employee signs and dates the job description for their position at hire and again when it is revised. The signed copy is kept in the personnel file (PER-03). Job descriptions list essential functions and are written and applied in line with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Qualified applicants and employees with disabilities are offered reasonable accommodation unless it would cause undue hardship, and requests are handled under the personnel policies and kept confidential.

The Agency Director reviews all job descriptions at least annually, with the annual performance evaluation (PER-04) and annual program evaluation (ADM-08). Job descriptions are revised when duties or regulatory requirements change.

MINIMUM CONTENT BY POSITION. Agency Director: meets the 10A NCAC 13J .1001 standard (ADM-04); manages operations, governing body reporting, personnel, finances, compliance and DHSR communications. RN/Service Supervisor: see ADM-06. Scheduler/Intake Coordinator: takes referrals, performs the intake screen, matches aides to client plans, schedules visits, manages missed-visit procedures (CLN-19), handles timekeeping and EVV records (MED-03), and maintains confidentiality; does not make clinical decisions. In-Home Aide: meets PER-01 qualifications; provides only the tasks in the client's plan of care that the aide has demonstrated; documents each visit; reports changes in condition, incidents and suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation (CLN-14, CLN-15, CLN-20); follows infection control (ADM-10) and boundary rules (PER-09). Other positions: described in writing in the same format before the position is filled.

definitions.definition: A written statement of a position's title, reporting line, qualifications and specific responsibilities.
The fundamental duties of a position, as used under the ADA.
A change in the job or work setting that lets a qualified person with a disability perform the essential functions, unless it causes undue hardship.

procedures: The Agency Director drafts a job description for each position before the agency recruits or accepts any applicant for it, using the standard template with title, reporting line, qualifications, essential functions and responsibilities.
The Agency Director confirms that each job description matches the licensure rules and this manual: ADM-04 for the director, ADM-06 for the Service Supervisor and PER-01 for aides.
The governing body reviews and approves the set of job descriptions at adoption of this manual and after any change.
The Agency Director gives the applicant the job description for the position being applied for before an offer is made, so the applicant knows the qualifications and essential functions.

On the first day of work, before the employee is assigned any client duties, the supervisor reviews the job description with the employee, answers questions and obtains the employee's signature and date.
The Agency Director files the signed job description in the employee's personnel file (PER-03) the same day it is signed.
The Agency Director or Service Supervisor checks each assignment against the job description and the employee's documented training, competency and license before the schedule is released.
No employee is assigned a task that is outside the job description. A temporary change of duties requires a written assignment by the Agency Director and documented competency (PER-02).

If an employee or applicant requests an accommodation under the ADA, the Agency Director meets with the person, reviews the essential functions, considers reasonable accommodations and documents the outcome in a confidential file kept separate from the personnel file.
The Agency Director reviews every job description at least once a year during the performance evaluation cycle (PER-04) and notes the review date on the document.

When a job description is revised, the Agency Director gives the revised version to each affected employee within 10 working days. The employee signs and dates it, and the signed copy replaces the old one in the file. The old version is kept for the record.
During the annual program evaluation (ADM-08) and the personnel record review (PRR-01), the reviewer checks that every employee has a signed, current job description.
Missing or outdated job descriptions are corrected at once, and the correction is recorded in the review report.

responsibilities.duty: Approves job descriptions and reviews them at adoption and when positions change.
Writes and updates job descriptions, obtains signatures, handles accommodation requests and checks assignments against the job description.
Reviews aide job descriptions with aides, assigns only demonstrated tasks and reports mismatches to the Agency Director.
Read, sign and follow the job description for their position and ask for clarification when a duty is unclear.

documentation: Current job description for every position
Employee-signed and dated job description in each personnel file
Record of annual review and revision dates
Confidential accommodation records (kept separate from the personnel file)
Annual program evaluation and personnel record review findings on job descriptions

policies.title: Annual Program Evaluation and Quality Improvement
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Director, Service Supervisor and other staff who take part in the evaluation
policies.purpose: To have the governing body complete a documented comprehensive evaluation of the agency's program every year, and to use the findings to improve services, staffing and compliance.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Administrative Policies item .1004(a,b,c&e), Annual program evaluation policy, 10A NCAC 13J .1004, and item A(9), program evaluation, 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a)(9).

The governing body of [AGENCY NAME] completes a comprehensive evaluation of the agency's total program once every year. The evaluation reviews at least: (1) the clients served, including numbers and characteristics; (2) the hours or units of service provided; (3) client outcomes; (4) the adequacy of staffing, including RN availability and aide capacity; (5) requests for service that were not accepted, and why; and (6) the reasons clients were discharged or services were discontinued. The evaluation also considers client complaints and incidents, results of the 90-day record reviews (ADM-09), supervisory visit findings, infection control and exposure events, personnel and training compliance, and Medicaid billing and EVV compliance where applicable.

The written report names the evaluators, describes the methods used (for example record sampling, client satisfaction surveys, data reports and staff input), records the findings, and states the corrective actions taken, who is responsible and the target date. Findings are used for performance improvement, and the follow-up is verified in the next review. This policy is one of the policies that the governing body adopts under 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a).

definitions.definition: The annual written review by the governing body of the agency's total program, services and outcomes.
