Orientation Completion Record with date, topics, trainer and signatures
Signed confidentiality agreement
Signed job description
Bloodborne pathogen training record
Hepatitis B vaccine record or declination
Core skills verification (as applicable)
Quiz or return-demonstration results

policies.title: Criminal Background Investigation and HCPR Check
policies.applies_to: All applicants, employees and contract staff who would provide services to clients or have access to clients, their homes or their records
policies.purpose: To protect clients by screening every applicant for criminal history and for a substantiated finding on the NC Health Care Personnel Registry (HCPR) before the person works for [AGENCY NAME].
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] submits the criminal history check request within 5 business days of a conditional offer of employment, as G.S. 131E-265 requires. The agency does not hire, directly or by contract, anyone with a substantiated finding on the HCPR. Results are kept in the personnel file. The HCPR can be reached at 919-855-3968. No one is assigned to a client until the criminal history result and HCPR check have been received and reviewed by the Agency Director. This policy meets Personnel Policies: G.S. 131E-265 (Criminal background investigation policy).

definitions.definition: An offer of employment or contract work that depends on completing screening, including the criminal history check and HCPR check.
The DHSR registry of substantiated findings of abuse, neglect, exploitation, misappropriation and similar findings against health care personnel.
A finding listed on the HCPR after the state review process. A person with a substantiated finding may not be hired by the agency.
The criminal record check requested under G.S. 131E-265 before a person starts work.

procedures: The Agency Director or designee tells each applicant, in the job posting and at the interview, that employment depends on a criminal history check and an HCPR check. The applicant signs a consent for both before the offer is final.

When the agency makes a conditional offer, the Agency Director or designee enters the date in the applicant's personnel record and sets the deadline for submitting the criminal history check request: 5 business days from that date.

The designee submits the criminal history check request through the process required by the State for G.S. 131E-265, and records the date of submission, the person who submitted it and any confirmation number. If the request is not submitted by day 5, the Agency Director is told the same day and the offer does not proceed until the reason is documented and the request is submitted.

The designee checks the HCPR for the applicant before the first day of work, using the HCPR contact, 919-855-3968, or the HCPR online listing if available, and records the date, the result and the name of the person who checked. The checks are repeated at least once a year, at the time of the annual evaluation (PER-04).

If the applicant has a substantiated finding on the HCPR, the Agency Director withdraws the conditional offer. The agency does not hire the person directly or by contract, including through a staffing agency or a subcontract (CLN-09).

The Agency Director personally reviews every criminal history result when it is received. If a result shows a conviction or pending charge, the Agency Director considers the nature and date of the offense, its relation to client care and the duties of the position, and any other information provided by the applicant, and records the decision and reasons in writing. The review is done consistently for all applicants and in line with CLN-17.

No applicant is scheduled for client care, shadowing in a client home, or access to client records until the Agency Director has signed the screening clearance showing that the criminal history result and HCPR check were received and reviewed.
The designee also checks the Nurse Aide Registry and any applicable professional license status (see PER-01) and files these together with the criminal history and HCPR results.

The designee files the criminal history result, the HCPR check record, the signed consent and the Agency Director's clearance in the personnel file (PER-03), in a section with limited access (ADM-15).

If a staff member is arrested or charged with an offense or learns of a substantiated finding, the staff member must tell the Agency Director in writing within 1 business day. The Agency Director removes the staff member from client assignments while the matter is reviewed and decides on employment action.

If the agency learns of an allegation involving abuse, neglect, exploitation or misappropriation by a staff member, it follows CLN-14 and CLN-11. The staff member is removed from client contact during the investigation.
The Agency Director confirms that every contract staff member or staffing agency used has met the same screening, and obtains written proof from the contractor before assignment (CLN-09).

The Agency Director reviews the screening dates for all new hires every quarter, and any gap between the conditional offer and the submission of the criminal history request is corrected and reported in the annual program evaluation (ADM-08).
The personnel records custodian audits each new personnel file against the Personnel Record Review Checklist (PRR-01) to confirm screening items are present.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews every result, signs screening clearance, decides on any criminal history findings and withdraws any offer where the HCPR shows a substantiated finding.
Obtains consent, submits the criminal history request within 5 business days of the conditional offer, runs the HCPR check and files the results.
Does not schedule anyone without the Agency Director's signed clearance.
Gives accurate information, signs the consent and reports any arrest, charge or HCPR matter to the Agency Director within 1 business day.

documentation: Signed consent for criminal history and HCPR checks
Conditional offer date and criminal history request submission record
Criminal history result
HCPR check record (date, result, who checked) and annual re-check
Agency Director's written review and screening clearance
Contractor screening proof
Personnel Record Review Checklist

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
policies.applies_to: All employees of [AGENCY NAME], especially in-home aides, service supervisors and any non-exempt office staff, and the administrator, payroll and scheduling staff who set and record their pay
policies.purpose: To make sure every employee is paid for all time worked, at no less than the minimum wage and with overtime when required, and that [AGENCY NAME] complies with the federal, state and local law that 10A NCAC 13J .0906 requires it to follow.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] complies with the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), 29 CFR Part 552 and North Carolina wage and hour law. [AGENCY NAME] is a third-party employer of home care workers. It therefore does not claim the companionship-services or live-in exemptions, and it pays 1.5 times the regular rate of pay for all hours worked over 40 in a workweek. Aides are paid no less than the applicable minimum wage; the North Carolina state minimum wage is $7.25 per hour, and the higher federal, state or local rate applies if one is in effect. Travel time between clients during the workday and other compensable time (orientation, training, in-service, required meetings, on-call time that restricts personal use of time) is counted as hours worked. Aides are classified as employees, not independent contractors. No manager may ask, permit or pressure an employee to work off the clock. This policy supports the compliance-with-laws requirement of 10A NCAC 13J .0906.

definitions.definition: A fixed, recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods) that [AGENCY NAME] designates in writing for payroll. Overtime is calculated on each workweek separately.
All time an employee is required or permitted to work, including client visits, travel between clients, required training, orientation, meetings and documentation time.
The hourly rate of pay plus other required non-discretionary pay, used to calculate overtime at 1.5 times.
An employer other than the client or the client's family or household that employs the home care worker. Third-party employers may not use the companionship or live-in exemptions.
An employee who must be paid at least minimum wage and overtime for hours over 40 in a workweek.

procedures: At hire, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] classifies each position in writing as non-exempt or exempt. All in-home aide positions are classified as non-exempt employees. The classification is recorded in the job description (ADM-07) and the personnel record (PER-03).

[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] designates one fixed workweek (for example, Sunday 12:00 a.m. through Saturday 11:59 p.m.) and gives it in writing to all employees and to payroll. The workweek may be changed only in writing and not to avoid overtime.

At hire, the employee receives a written statement of the hourly rate, the workweek, the pay period and payday, and how travel time and overtime are paid. The employee signs it, and a copy is filed in the personnel record.

Payroll verifies before each payroll that every aide's hourly rate is at least the $7.25 North Carolina minimum wage and at least any higher federal or local minimum that applies. Any rate below the minimum is corrected before pay is issued.

Aides record time worked through the timekeeping and EVV system (MED-03) for visits and on the agency timesheet for time not captured by EVV (orientation, training, meetings, travel not recorded in EVV). Aides are told that all time must be recorded and that they will be paid for it.

Travel time between one client's home and the next client's home during the workday is counted as hours worked and paid at the aide's hourly rate. Ordinary commuting from the aide's home to the first client and from the last client to home is not counted unless the aide is sent first to the office or another work site, or other federal rules make it compensable.

Time spent in orientation (PER-06), required competency validation (PER-02), in-service education (PER-05), required staff meetings and required supervisory visits is counted as hours worked and paid.

No automatic deductions are taken for meals, sleep or breaks. If an assignment includes a long shift, an overnight shift or a bona fide meal break, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews the federal rules before scheduling it and documents any agreed deduction in writing in advance. [AGENCY NAME] does not schedule live-in arrangements under a companionship or live-in exemption.

Each pay period, payroll adds all hours worked in the workweek (client hours, compensable travel and other compensable time). Hours over 40 in a workweek are paid at 1.5 times the regular rate. Overtime is never offset by shortening the following week.

The scheduler (CLN-19) reviews each aide's scheduled and worked hours at least once during the workweek. When an aide is projected to reach 40 hours, the scheduler notifies [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] before additional hours are assigned, so overtime is authorized and budgeted in advance. Overtime that was worked is paid even if it was not authorized, and the supervisor handles the unauthorized overtime through the discipline process.

Medicaid authorized hours, billing units and client rates do not limit what an aide is paid. Aides are paid for all hours actually worked, including hours that cannot be billed. Payroll flags any such hours for [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] to review (MED-01, MED-03).

Payroll reconciles EVV visit records and manual timesheets to payroll hours each pay period. Differences are resolved with the aide and supervisor, documented, and corrected in the next payroll at the latest.

Managers may not edit an employee's time to reduce hours. Any edit to recorded time requires a reason, the employee's acknowledgment where practical, and a supervisor's signature or system-recorded approval.

Employees who believe they were not paid correctly report it to payroll or [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. The matter is reviewed within the next pay period and any underpayment is paid promptly. No employee is retaliated against for raising a wage or hour concern.

[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews payroll classifications, the minimum wage rate and overtime practice at least annually and when federal or state law changes, and records the review in the policy review log (ADM-16).

Payroll records (time records, rates, hours, overtime, deductions and pay dates) are kept for each employee and are available for inspection by the agency's authorized government reviewers. They are kept for at least three years.

responsibilities.duty: Classifies positions, designates the workweek, approves overtime, reviews pay practice annually and ensures compliance with 10A NCAC 13J .0906 and wage laws.
Calculates hours worked including compensable travel, applies the 1.5 times overtime rate, checks the minimum wage and reconciles EVV, timesheets and payroll.
Reviews timesheets, ensures aides record all time and never directs off-the-clock work.
Record all hours worked accurately, report pay concerns and do not perform unrecorded work.

documentation: Written position classifications and signed pay statement in each personnel record
Timesheets, EVV records, payroll registers and overtime approvals
Payroll reconciliation records
Annual wage-and-hour compliance review entry in the policy review log

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, contract staff, students and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME] who have contact with clients, their homes, their records or their property
policies.purpose: To protect clients' dignity, privacy, property and safety, and to set clear standards of conduct and professional boundaries for all staff, consistent with the client rights in G.S. 131E-144.3 and the written personnel policies required by 10A NCAC 13J .1003(d)-(e).
policies.policy: Staff of [AGENCY NAME] treat every client with dignity and respect and keep a professional relationship. Staff do not accept gifts or money from clients, do not use client property for personal purposes, do not post about clients on social media, and do not smoke in the client's home (G.S. 131E-143; see CLN-07). Staff do not perform tasks they are not trained, competent and licensed for. Violations lead to discipline up to and including termination, and may require a report to the Health Care Personnel Registry (HCPR). Staff are told of this policy at orientation and sign an acknowledgment. This policy implements the client rights to dignity and privacy, confidentiality, and freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation in G.S. 131E-144.3, and the personnel policy and job description requirements of 10A NCAC 13J .1003(d)-(e).

definitions.definition: The limit between a helpful professional relationship and a personal, social, financial or exploitative one.
Money, goods, services, favors or a financial benefit of any value offered by or to a client or family, other than a token item allowed by this policy.
Anything belonging to the client or household: home, vehicle, phone, computer, food, supplies, tools, medications, financial and personal items.
Any online platform for posting or sharing text, photos, video or messages, including texting groups and review sites.
The NC Health Care Personnel Registry maintained by DHSR, which records substantiated findings against health care personnel.

procedures: At orientation (PER-06), the Service Supervisor reviews this policy with each new employee, answers questions, and obtains a signed acknowledgment that is filed in the personnel record (PER-03).

Gifts: Staff do not accept or ask for money, gifts, loans, tips, food or services of value from clients or family members. If a gift is offered, the staff member politely declines, explains the agency policy, and tells the Service Supervisor the same day. The supervisor documents the offer in the client record.

Staff do not borrow from or lend to clients, make purchases for personal benefit, sell products or services to clients, ask clients to sign documents or accept being named in a will, trust, power of attorney, or beneficiary designation. Any such request is reported to the Service Supervisor immediately and handled under CLN-16.

Personal use of client property: Staff do not use client's vehicle, phone, computer, television, food, supplies, medications, keys, credit/debit cards, bank accounts or other property for personal reasons. Staff may use the client's telephone or bathroom only if the client permits and only for work needs or personal necessity.

Social media and recording: Staff do not post, share, message or comment about clients, their homes, their conditions or their families on social media or any public or private group. Staff do not take or share photographs, video or audio of clients or their homes unless the client signs a written consent and the administrator approves it for a documented care purpose. Staff do not accept client friend requests while employed.
Confidentiality: Staff discuss clients only with the care team and only as needed for care, in line with ADM-15. Staff do not discuss one client with another.
Smoking and tobacco: Staff do not smoke, vape or use tobacco in a client's home, as required by G.S. 131E-143 and CLN-07. Staff do not leave a client unattended to smoke.

Relationships: Staff do not enter into romantic, sexual, business or financial relationships with clients. Staff do not share personal problems with clients or ask clients for personal favors. Staff do not provide personal contact information beyond what is needed for scheduling.

Impairment and conduct: Staff do not work under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs, or while impaired by medication that affects safe performance. Staff do not bring family, friends, children or pets to a client visit and do not allow others to attend without the client's and supervisor's permission.

Scope: Staff perform only the tasks on the client's plan of care and permitted by CLN-13. They do not accept instructions from the client or family to perform tasks outside their training, competence or license, and they call the Service Supervisor or on-call RN when asked to do so, as required by 10A NCC 13J .1003(d)-(e) duty assignment.

Reporting: Staff report any boundary concern, gift offer, suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation to the Service Supervisor immediately and follow CLN-14. Reports may be made without fear of reprisal.

Investigation: When a violation is alleged, the Service Supervisor notifies the administrator the same day. The administrator opens a written investigation, interviews the employee and the client or witnesses, and may remove the employee from the client's case pending the result. Client dignity, safety and grievance rights under G.S. 131E-144.3 are protected throughout, and the client or family is told the outcome that affects them.

Discipline: Based on the finding, the administrator issues a documented corrective action: coaching, written warning, suspension or termination. Misappropriation of client property, abuse, neglect or exploitation results in immediate removal from client contact and may result in termination.

HCPR reporting: If the conduct is an allegation of abuse, neglect, misappropriation of client property or another reportable act, the administrator makes the HCPR report within the timeframes in CLN-11 and keeps the investigation file.
The administrator reviews this policy annually and records the review in ADM-16. Substantiated violations are reviewed in the annual program evaluation (ADM-08) to identify training needs.

responsibilities.duty: Enforces the policy, directs investigations, imposes discipline and makes HCPR reports.
Teaches this policy, monitors boundaries during supervisory visits, documents gift offers and refers concerns to the administrator.
Follow this policy, report concerns and decline gifts, personal use of property, social media posting and smoking in client homes.

documentation: Signed policy acknowledgment in personnel record
Gift-offer and boundary-concern notes in client record
Investigation file, discipline records and HCPR report copies
Annual policy review entry

policies.title: Personnel Record Review Checklist for Surveyors
policies.applies_to: Personnel files of all employees and contract staff of [AGENCY NAME], used by the administrator for internal audit and by DHSR surveyors during review
policies.purpose: To give [AGENCY NAME] and surveyors a single checklist for reviewing each personnel file against 10A NCAC 13J .1003(c), (d)-(e), (f) and (g) and G.S. 131E-265, and to confirm that no staff member is assigned to client care until the file is complete.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete personnel file for every employee and contract staff member and audits each file against the checklist in this policy at hire, at least annually and before any DHSR survey. Each file must contain: the application; a signed job description; references; TB records; Hepatitis B vaccine record or declination; annual bloodborne and airborne pathogen training; annual evaluation; credential checks; and competency verification (10A NCAC 13J .1003(f)). The file must show that the criminal history check request was submitted within 5 business days of the conditional offer (G.S. 131E-265) and that the HCPR check found no substantiated finding (10A NCAC 13J .1003(c)). Each aide must be listed on the Nurse Aide Registry or, if hired after 4/1/2009 and not listed, have the six core skills verified by an RN (10A NCAC 13J .1003(g)). In-service attendance records are kept (10A NCAC 13J .1003(d)-(e)). Files are kept for 1 year after termination.

definitions.definition: An offer of employment contingent on completion of the criminal history check, HCPR check and other pre-employment requirements.
The state registry listing nurse aides who have completed required training and competency evaluation.
The six skills an RN must verify for an aide not on the Nurse Aide Registry: mobility/transfers, bath/shower, toileting, dressing, eating and continence care.
Verification, before assignment and as required afterward, that a staff member holds the current license, certification or registry listing required for the duties assigned.
A documented review of one personnel file against the checklist, signed and dated by the reviewer.

procedures: The administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) assigns a reviewer (administrator or designee who is not the employee) to audit every file when the employee is hired, once a year no later than the employee's anniversary month, and at least before each DHSR survey or inspection.
The reviewer uses the checklist form in this policy, one per employee, and records the employee's name, position, hire date, date conditional offer made, date of review and reviewer's signature.
Item 1, Application: Confirm a completed, signed and dated application is in the file, with work history and the licenses or certifications the applicant claims.
Item 2, Job description: Confirm the signed and dated job description for the employee's position is in the file and matches the duties assigned (10A NCAC 13J .1003(d)-(e)).
Item 3, References: Confirm references were obtained and documented (name, date, who contacted, result) before the employee was assigned to a client.

Item 4, Criminal history: Confirm the date of the conditional offer and the date the criminal history check request was submitted. The request must be made within 5 business days of the conditional offer (G.S. 131E-265). Confirm the result is in the file and that any disqualifying or concerning result was reviewed by the administrator and documented before assignment.

Item 5, HCPR check: Confirm the HCPR check was run before hire and that the file shows no substantiated finding. A person with a substantiated finding is not hired, directly or by contract (10A NCAC 13J .1003(c)). Confirm contract staff have the same documentation.

Item 6, Nurse Aide Registry or core skills: For each aide, confirm Nurse Aide Registry listing (printout or verification with date). If the aide was hired after 4/1/2009 and is not listed, confirm there is an RN-signed record verifying all six core skills: mobility/transfers, bath/shower, toileting, dressing, eating and continence care (10A NCAC 13J .1003(g)).

Item 7, Credential checks: For licensed staff (RN, LPN, other), confirm primary-source verification of current NC license and the next renewal date. Calendar the expiration so it is re-verified before it lapses. No one is assigned to duties for which they are not trained, competent and licensed.
Item 8, Competency verification: Confirm skills validation and competency documentation for the duties the employee performs, signed and dated by the evaluator (PER-02, 10A NCAC 13J .1003(f)).
Item 9, TB records: Confirm TB screening/testing records are in the file and current per ADM-12.
Item 10, Hepatitis B: Confirm the Hepatitis B vaccine record or a signed declination is in the file (ADM-13).

Item 11, Annual training: Confirm documentation of annual bloodborne pathogen and airborne pathogen training for each employee (ADM-11, 10A NCAC 13J .1003(f)). Confirm in-service attendance records are in the file or in the central in-service log (PER-05). No hour count is set by the rule, so compare against the agency's own in-service plan.
Item 12, Annual evaluation: Confirm an annual performance evaluation is in the file for each employee employed 12 months or longer (PER-04).
Item 13, Orientation: Confirm orientation record is signed and dated by employee and trainer, with topics covered (PER-06).
Record every missing, expired or late item as a deficiency on the checklist. The reviewer gives the list to the administrator the same day.

The administrator assigns a correction owner and due date (for missing or expired TB, vaccine, evaluation, training or credential items, the due date is within [NUMBER] days) and removes the employee from client assignments if a pre-assignment requirement (criminal history, HCPR, registry listing or core skills, references, credential) is missing.

After correction, the reviewer re-checks the item, signs and dates, and files the completed checklist in the personnel record. Terminated staff files are kept for 1 year after termination (10A NCAC 13J .1003(f)) and then handled under PER-03.
The administrator summarizes audit findings for the annual program evaluation (ADM-08) and provides the completed checklists and files to the DHSR surveyor on request.

Completes the checklist for each file accurately, dates and signs it and reports deficiencies.

policies.title: Medicaid State Plan PCS (Clinical Coverage Policy 3L): Authorization and Service Plan
policies.applies_to: Administrator, intake staff, schedulers, billing staff, Registered Nurse and Service Supervisors providing or managing Medicaid State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) in the home
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] provides and bills Medicaid State Plan PCS only with a valid service authorization and an approved provider service plan, and never schedules beyond authorized hours, as required by NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 3L.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides Medicaid State Plan PCS under NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 3L (amended Jan. 1, 2026). PCS in the home requires a service authorization for a set number of hours and an approved provider service plan before services start. [AGENCY NAME] does not schedule beyond authorized hours. Authorization dates and hours are tracked for each client. The Medicaid PCS rate is $7.03 per unit (code 99509, HA/HB) effective Aug. 1, 2026; the unit length is confirmed on the NC Medicaid fee schedule before billing. PCS visits are verified through electronic visit verification (MED-03), consistent with 42 USC 1396b(l).

definitions.definition: The approval from NC Medicaid or its designee for a specified number of PCS hours for a specified period for a specific beneficiary.
The agency's written plan for delivering the authorized PCS tasks to the client, approved as required by Clinical Coverage Policy 3L.
The maximum hours that may be scheduled and billed within the authorization period.
The billing increment for code 99509 as set on the NC Medicaid fee schedule. The rate of $7.03 per unit applies from Aug. 1, 2026.
The log or system report showing each client's authorized hours, start and end dates, hours scheduled, hours used and reauthorization due date.

procedures: At referral (CLN-04), intake staff verify the client's active Medicaid eligibility and that the client has been assessed and approved for PCS. Intake staff obtain a copy of the service authorization showing the number of hours, effective dates and the provider named. If there is no authorization, intake staff tell the client or referral source that PCS cannot start until one is issued, and offer private pay options or referrals (CLN-03).

Before the first visit, the administrator confirms the authorization matches the client, the service and the provider. The authorization is entered in the authorization tracker with hours per period, start date, end date and the date the reauthorization request must begin.

The Registered Nurse conducts the initial in-home assessment and develops the plan of care (CLN-05, CLN-06). The administrator or RN prepares the provider service plan based on the assessment and authorization, listing the PCS tasks, frequency and hours.

The provider service plan is reviewed with the client or representative, who signs to show participation. The plan is submitted or approved as Clinical Coverage Policy 3L requires, and approval is filed in the client record before services begin. No visit is made before the authorization and approved plan are on file.

The scheduler (CLN-19) schedules only within the authorized hours and period. Scheduling software is set with the authorized hours as a cap where possible, and the scheduler checks the tracker before adding any visit.

The scheduler runs the authorization tracker weekly and compares hours scheduled and used with hours authorized. When a client reaches 80 percent of authorized hours in the period, the scheduler notifies the Service Supervisor and administrator.

[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] starts the reauthorization process at least [NUMBER] days before the authorization ends, following NC Medicaid's current process. The RN completes any required reassessment or documentation. The date and result of each request are recorded in the tracker.

If the client needs more hours than authorized, the Service Supervisor or RN tells the client and refers them to the proper channel to request a change in authorization. The agency does not exceed authorized hours in the meantime.

The agency does not bill Medicaid for hours not authorized, not delivered or not verified. The agency does not bill the Medicaid client for any Medicaid-covered service or for hours beyond the authorization, unless the client voluntarily elects separate private-pay services under a written service agreement (CLN-18).

Before each billing cycle, billing staff match each claim to the authorization (client, dates, hours), the EVV visit record and the aide's timesheet. Hours that are not supported are held, investigated and corrected (MED-03).

Billing staff confirm the rate and unit length on the current NC Medicaid fee schedule at the start of each billing period and whenever NC Medicaid announces a rate change. The $7.03 per unit rate effective Aug. 1, 2026 is applied to dates of service on or after that date. The administrator documents the check.

The Service Supervisor performs supervisory visits (CLN-08) and the 90-day plan of care review (CLN-06, ADM-09) to confirm services match the plan and authorization. Changes in condition (CLN-20) are reported to the RN and, when they may affect the authorization, to the appropriate Medicaid contact.
When an authorization ends and is not renewed, or the client is discharged, the administrator follows CLN-10 for notice and discharge planning and closes the tracker entry.

The administrator reviews the authorization tracker and a sample of claims monthly, documents errors found and corrects them, and includes results in the annual program evaluation (ADM-08) and compliance program (ADM-17).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures no services start without an authorization and approved plan, oversees reauthorization and billing accuracy.
Verify eligibility, obtain authorizations and enter them in the tracker.
Schedules only within authorized hours and dates, and runs weekly tracker checks.
Assesses the client, develops the plan of care and provider service plan, and completes reassessment documents.

policies.title: CAP/DA Waiver Coordination and HCBS Settings Requirements
policies.applies_to: Administrator, intake staff, Registered Nurse, Service Supervisors, schedulers and aides serving clients enrolled in the NC Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)
policies.purpose: To describe how [AGENCY NAME] coordinates in-home aide services for CAP/DA participants under the governing waiver, follows person-centered planning and home and community-based services (HCBS) setting requirements, and avoids dependence on any single payer.
policies.policy: CAP/DA is the Medicaid 1915(c) waiver (CMS 0132.R08.00, Nov. 1, 2024 through Oct. 31, 2029) that covers in-home aide services for adults at risk of institutionalization. Referrals and assessments run through NCLIFTSS (833-522-5429). [AGENCY NAME] provides CAP/DA services only to participants who are authorized and referred through the waiver process, follows the person-centered service plan, and respects the HCBS setting requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c): the participant's choice, dignity, privacy, autonomy and community access. [AGENCY NAME] does not depend on CAP/DA alone for census and maintains a mix of CAP/DA, State Plan PCS and private-pay clients.

definitions.definition: The Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults, a Medicaid home and community-based services waiver for adults who would otherwise need institutional care.
The entity that manages CAP/DA referrals and assessments, reached at 833-522-5429.
The plan for the participant's services, developed with and directed by the participant, reflecting the participant's goals, preferences and needs.
Federal requirements in 42 CFR 441.301(c) that waiver services be delivered in settings that support the participant's choice, privacy, dignity, autonomy and integration in the community.
The distribution of the agency's clients across Medicaid State Plan PCS, CAP/DA and private pay.

procedures: The administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) confirms that [AGENCY NAME] is enrolled and approved as a CAP/DA in-home aide provider before accepting any CAP/DA referral. The administrator records the enrollment date and keeps enrollment documents on file.

When an individual asks about CAP/DA, intake staff explain that referral and assessment run through NCLIFTSS (833-522-5429), give the number and help the person contact it. [AGENCY NAME] does not determine eligibility. Intake staff tell the individual that waiting lists or capacity limits may apply and offer State Plan PCS or private pay information and community referrals (CLN-03).

On receipt of a CAP/DA referral, intake staff verify the participant's waiver eligibility, the authorized services and amount, the dates of approval and the case manager or care advisor contact. Information is entered in the client record and authorization tracker (MED-01 process).

Intake staff confirm that the participant chooses [AGENCY NAME] as provider, and document the participant's choice and that the participant was informed of their right to choose or change providers. No pressure is placed on a participant to select or stay with [AGENCY NAME].

The Registered Nurse completes the in-home assessment and plan of care visit (CLN-05, CLN-06) and obtains and reviews the participant's person-centered service plan. The agency's plan of care reflects the participant's goals, schedule preferences, tasks and cultural and language needs.

The participant, and any representative the participant chooses, take part in developing and approving the plan of care and sign it. Plan changes are made with the participant and communicated to the case manager or care advisor.
Aides serve only the tasks and hours in the service plan and authorization. The scheduler does not schedule beyond authorized hours, and EVV is used for every CAP/DA visit (MED-03).

HCBS setting practices: Staff respect the participant's choices about daily schedule, food, visitors, privacy and use of their home. Staff knock and ask before entering rooms, protect privacy during personal care, and do not restrict the participant's movement, access to their belongings, visitors or the community. Any proposed restriction or modification must come through the person-centered plan process and not be done by aides.

Staff do not enforce agency convenience rules that limit the participant's autonomy, and they follow CLN-01 (rights), CLN-14 (abuse/neglect) and CLN-16 (property). The Service Supervisor checks HCBS practices during each supervisory visit (CLN-08) and records them.

The Service Supervisor or RN communicates with the case manager or care advisor at the 90-day plan review (CLN-06, ADM-09), and whenever the participant's condition or needs change (CLN-20), a hospitalization or ER visit occurs, a missed visit pattern develops (CLN-19) or an incident occurs (CLN-15). Communication is documented with date, contact and result.
The agency notifies the case manager or care advisor and the participant, following CLN-10, before any discharge, transfer or discontinuation, so the participant is not left without services.
Billing staff match CAP/DA claims to the service authorization and EVV record before submission (MED-01, MED-03) and use the Medicaid rate in effect for the date of service.

The administrator tracks payer mix each quarter. If CAP/DA or any one payer represents more than [PERCENT] percent of census or revenue, the administrator documents a plan to diversify through private-pay marketing, State Plan PCS and community referrals. The administrator does not plan staffing or budget on the assumption that CAP/DA referrals will fill capacity.

The administrator reviews waiver requirements, program changes and the waiver term (ending Oct. 31, 2029) at least annually, updates this policy through ADM-16, and reports results in the annual program evaluation (ADM-08).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains CAP/DA enrollment, oversees compliance with waiver and HCBS settings requirements and monitors payer mix.
Direct individuals to NCLIFTSS, verify waiver authorization, and document participant choice of provider.
Develops the plan of care in line with the person-centered plan and coordinates with the case manager or care advisor.
Monitors HCBS practices and coordination during supervisory visits and plan reviews.
Deliver only the planned services, respect participant choice, privacy and autonomy, and report concerns.

documentation: CAP/DA enrollment documents and service authorization copies
Participant provider-choice documentation and signed plan of care
Copy of the person-centered service plan and case manager contacts
Supervisory visit notes on HCBS setting practices
Payer-mix tracking and annual review records

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
policies.applies_to: Aides, schedulers, Service Supervisors, payroll and billing staff and the administrator for all Medicaid State Plan PCS and CAP/DA visits
policies.purpose: To ensure every Medicaid PCS and CAP/DA visit is captured by electronic visit verification (EVV) as the 21st Century Cures Act requires, that manual entries stay within the state limit, and that EVV, authorizations, timekeeping and claims agree.
policies.policy: EVV is required for Medicaid PCS and CAP/DA visits. [AGENCY NAME] captures at least 85 percent of visit data electronically; manual entries must be 15 percent or less. [AGENCY NAME] uses Sandata, the state vendor for NC Medicaid Direct, and for clients covered by a health plan that contracts with the agency, the plan's EVV solution. Weekly exception reports are run and EVV records, authorizations and claims are reconciled before billing. Falsifying or altering visit data is prohibited and is handled under ADM-17 and PER-09. This policy follows 42 USC 1396b(l).

definitions.definition: Electronic visit verification: a system that electronically records the type of service, the individual receiving the service, the individual providing it, the date, the location and the start and end times of the visit.
A visit record created or edited by staff rather than captured electronically at the visit.
A system report listing visits with missing, late, mismatched or manually edited data, or visits outside the authorization.
The state EVV vendor for NC Medicaid Direct.
Matching each EVV visit record to the service authorization, the aide's payroll time and the claim.

procedures: At hire and before the first visit, the Service Supervisor trains each aide on the EVV system used for the client's payer: how to clock in and out at the client's home, what to do if the device or connection fails, and the rule that visits must not be falsified. The training is documented and filed in the personnel record.

The administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) confirms for each Medicaid client whether the payer is NC Medicaid Direct (Sandata) or a health plan that requires its own EVV solution. The correct EVV system is assigned in the client record and the scheduling system.
The scheduler enters each client's visit in the EVV system only within the authorized hours and dates (MED-01, MED-02) and with the correct service and aide.

The aide records the start of the visit when arriving at the client's home and the end when leaving, using the system method assigned. The aide does not clock in before arrival, clock out after leaving or record a visit for someone else.

If the EVV system cannot capture the visit (device failure, no signal, system outage), the aide calls the Service Supervisor or scheduler during or immediately after the visit, and writes the actual start and end times, task notes and the reason on the visit note. The aide does not ask the client to record times for them.

A manual entry or edit may be made only by designated staff, only with a documented reason code and the aide's or supervisor's confirmation, and only within the time the system allows. Each edit is traceable to the person who made it. Staff do not edit times to match the schedule or the authorization.

The scheduler runs the EVV exception report at least weekly, on [DAY OF WEEK], and works each exception: missed clock-ins/outs, late entries, visits outside the authorization, unmatched aide/client, visit time differences and manual edits. Each is resolved or explained in writing within [NUMBER] business days.

The administrator calculates the percentage of visits captured electronically and the percentage entered manually each month, using system reports. If manual entries exceed 15 percent, or electronic capture falls below 85 percent, the administrator identifies the causes (aide, client location, device, connection, training), starts a corrective action plan and retrains the aides involved within [NUMBER] days. Results are recorded and reviewed in the annual program evaluation (ADM-08).

Before each billing cycle, billing staff reconcile each claim against the EVV visit record, the service authorization and the aide's payroll time. Claims are submitted only for visits that are verified, authorized and delivered. Any mismatch is held and investigated.

Payroll compares EVV records to payroll hours each pay period (PER-08). Time that is not captured by EVV, such as travel time between clients, orientation and training, is recorded on the agency timesheet and paid. EVV times do not replace the requirement to pay for all hours worked.

Supervisors review a sample of EVV records during supervisory visits and plan of care reviews (CLN-08, CLN-06) to confirm that visit times and tasks match the plan of care. Missed or short visits are documented and handled under CLN-19.

Aides who record false times, share logins, or alter visit data are removed from the case pending investigation, disciplined under PER-09, and if fraud is suspected, the administrator follows the compliance procedures in ADM-17.
EVV records contain client location and health-related information and are protected under ADM-15. Access is limited by role, passwords are not shared and logins are removed when an employee leaves.

The administrator keeps EVV records, exception reports and reconciliation records and makes them available to NC Medicaid and its authorized reviewers on request. They are kept according to the agency's records retention schedule (ADM-17).
The administrator reviews the EVV vendor requirements, any changes by NC Medicaid or contracted plans and this policy at least annually and records the review in ADM-16.

Enters visits within authorizations, runs and resolves weekly exception reports.
Trains aides on EVV, reviews visit records during supervision and addresses falsification concerns.
Reconcile EVV, authorizations, payroll and claims before billing and payment.
Record visits accurately at the client's home, report EVV failures immediately and never alter or share EVV data.

Monthly electronic-capture and manual-entry percentage reports and corrective action plans

Reconciliation records of EVV, authorizations, payroll and claims

official.notes: DHSR has no separate policy-manual form. The Home Care Initial Survey Checklist (Rev 9/21) is the review tool. Submission process: (1) The applicant mails the license application (hcapp.pdf), the fee, and proof of prior home care ownership or of DHSR-approved home care training to DHSR, 2712 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-2712. (2) DHSR emails to confirm receipt, then emails a request for the policies, procedures and personnel documents. (3) The initial survey is a desk review of those documents against the licensure rules. If no further information is needed, DHSR emails an approval letter with instructions for printing the license from the Enterprise system. Organize the manual in the checklist's order and group it under its three policy headings: Administrative Policies, Client Care Policies and Personnel Policies. Label each policy with the rule cite printed on the checklist so the surveyor can check each line. The checklist does not number its items, so item_id values above are built from the section name and rule cite. Cites are as printed on the checklist, including its '.1001 (5)' for emergency preparedness (the rule text places it at .1001(a)(5)). Three checklist lines also cover the Supporting Documentation section. Only the Agency Organization Chart is policy content and appears in the items above. The other Supporting Documentation lines are excluded as non-policy paperwork: proof of prior ownership, the training certificate, the premises lease, articles of incorporation, and the annual projected budget. The checklist has no cite for the bloodborne pathogen and Hepatitis B policy lines. Rule .1003(f)(5)-(6) covers Hepatitis B and pathogen training records. The checklist marks some items 'if applicable' (Companion Sitter Agency Director) or ties them to a service type (companion/sitter rules .1503-.1504). For a Personal Home Care (in-home aide) agency, the in-home aide cites (.1107, .1110) apply. The Personnel Record Review grid is a record check, not policy content. It covers the application, resume, signed job description, license verification, NA registry and Health Care Personnel Registry check, competency verification, TB proof, bloodborne pathogen training proof, Hepatitis B proof, orientation, reference checks, and signed criminal background consent. The checklist page was last modified in 2018, but the checklist PDF itself is Rev 9/21. Confirm with DHSR (919-855-4620, DHSR.homecare@dhhs.nc.gov) that no newer revision exists before submitting.
